key: And if anyone of the idolaters seeketh thy protection (O Muhammad), then protect him so that he may hear the Word of Allah, and afterward convey him to his place of safety. That is because they are a folk who know not.
s: After the order to slay the idolaters, the Prophet is told what to do when one of them asks for protection; al-Tabari, on 9:6, reads it as safety while he hears the Qur’an and, if he refuses Islam, safe passage home to his people.

evidence.words: فأمّنه حتى يسمع كلام الله وتتلوه عليه = ﴿ثم أبلغه مأمنه﴾ ، يقول: ثم رُدَّه بعد سماعه كلام الله إن هو أبَي أن يسلم، ولم يتعظ لما تلوته عليه من كلام الله فيؤمن = "إلى مأمنه"، يقول: إلى حيث يأمن منك وممن في طاعتك، حتى يلحق بداره وقومه من المشركين
evidence.gloss: Grant him safety until he hears the word of God as you recite it to him; ‘then convey him to his place of safety’: send him back, after he has heard God’s word, if he refuses to become a Muslim and is not moved to believe by what you recited to him; ‘to his place of safety’: to where he is safe from you and from those who obey you, until he reaches his home and his people among the idolaters.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, At-Tawbah 9:6, at 1240). Plain sense faithful: 9:5 orders the idolaters slain after the sacred months, 9:6 turns to the one who seeks protection; hard matter stated in one plain clause, no four-word run from the ayah. In the packet on 9:6 al-Tabari glosses the ayah in his own voice (qala Abu Jafar): the Word of Allah is the Qur’an, grant him safety until he hears it, and if he refuses Islam send him back to where he is safe, until he reaches his home and his people; he later holds the ayah unabrogated. The sentence carries exactly this, including the limit (safe passage home if he refuses), without drift. Proposer’s evidence re-copied character for character from the packet. entry-check ok.
